welcome.heading: Welcome to Soul Rhythm.
welcome.line1: A place to explore possibilities, perspectives, and ideas.
welcome.line2: Take a look around. There is lots to discover. There's no rush.
welcome.direct: Or, if you came looking for something specific, you can head there directly.

meetLori.label: MEET LORI
meetLori.heading: A short hello from Lori
meetLori.intro: Lori put together a few words of welcome. It takes about a minute. Watch now, or come back to it any time.
meetLori.transcript: Hi, I'm Lori. Welcome to Soul Rhythm. I made this place as a porch light — somewhere you can sit for a minute, look around, and see what stirs. There's no right way to wander. Come as you are.
meetLori.talk: If you'd like to talk, I'm here

journey.q1: What sort of experiences or activities fill you up?
journey.q2: What is it about that activity or experience that gives you energy?
journey.close: Sometimes all it takes is a moment to notice. And sometimes, that moment makes us curious about what might be possible. If you'd like to keep exploring, I'm here.
journey.finePrint: It can take as little or as much time as you have.

stories.heading: Soul Rhythm Stories is a place to settle in and explore.
stories.intro: Here you'll find stories and ideas that may make you wonder, think differently, discover something you didn't know, or simply leave you wanting to know more.
stories.empty: No stories match that just yet.
stories.storeNote: Store and checkout powered by WooCommerce or Shopify in the real build.
stories.whereNote: A recommendation — find it wherever you like to watch or read.

items.title: The Gift of Rest
items.author: Mara Ellison
items.line: A quiet invitation to reclaim unhurried time.
items.note: Lori comes back to this whenever the week starts to hurry her. It is a small book that makes more room.

items.title: Porch Light
items.author: James Whitaker
items.line: Essays on noticing what's already here.
items.note: These essays feel like sitting outside at dusk. Lori loves how they ask almost nothing of you except attention.

items.title: Finding Your Rhythm
items.author: Lena Ortiz
items.line: A field guide for living at a human pace.
items.note: Practical without being pushy. Lori keeps it on the study table for anyone who is ready to try a gentler tempo.

items.title: Letters from the Garden
items.author: Helen Brooks
items.line: Correspondence on growing and letting go.
items.note: Lori loves the patience in these letters — how they treat growing as a conversation, not a project.

items.title: Quiet Enough
items.author: Thomas Reed
items.line: A companion for nights when the house finally settles.
items.note: Not a how-to. Lori recommends it when someone needs company more than advice.

items.title: The Unhurried Life
items.author: Sofia Nguyen
items.line: Stories of people who chose a slower yes.
items.note: This is one of Lori's picks because it never scolds. It just shows what becomes possible when you stop rushing.

items.title: Still Waters
items.author: Amina Cole
items.line: A film about returning home and beginning again.
items.note: Lori loves the quiet middle of this film — the part where nothing big happens and everything changes.

items.title: The Long Walk Home
items.author: David Lang
items.line: Two friends, one road, many questions.
items.note: A Lori pick for anyone who thinks they need a map before they start. The conversation is the path.

items.title: Evening Light
items.author: Nora Hale
items.line: A short film about the last hour of an ordinary day.
items.note: Lori watches this when she wants to remember that ordinary hours are enough.

items.title: Morning Pages
items.author: Priya Shah
items.line: A short series on daily creative practice.
items.note: Gentle episodes. Lori likes that you can start on any morning and not feel behind.

items.title: Kitchen Table Talks
items.author: Evan Cole
items.line: Conversations that wander toward what matters.
items.note: These talks sound like they could have happened on Lori's porch. She keeps them close for that reason.

items.title: Porch Season
items.author: Clara West
items.line: A new series about staying put and looking again.
items.note: New on the shelf. Lori is still sitting with it — and already handing it to people who need permission to stay.

consulting.q2: Interesting. What makes this matter to you?
consulting.thanks: Thanks for sharing that. Ideas don't have to be finished before we talk about them.
